chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Musa ibn Ja'far, from Ahmad ibn Bishr, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Al-Battakhi, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who married a woman on the condition of teaching her a Chapter from the Book of Allah, then divorced her before consummating the marriage, with what does he have recourse upon her? He said: With half of what he would teach, similar to that Chapter.
ai.seo_question: What is the dower entitlement for a wife if divorced before consummation when the dower was teaching a Quranic chapter?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the flexibility of dower (mahr) in Shia jurisprudence, where knowledge of the Quran can serve as valid consideration. It clarifies that in cases of divorce prior to consummation, the husband must pay half the assessed value of the specific chapter taught, reflecting the principle that the dower is tied to the agreed-upon benefit rather than a fixed monetary sum. This ruling underscores the practical application of Quranic recitation as a tangible asset in marital contracts.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Musa Bin Ja’far, from Ahmad Bin Bishr, from Ali Bin Asbaat, from Al Battakhiya, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Zurara,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> regarding a man who married a woman upon (a dower of teaching her) a Chapter from the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, then divorced her before he copulated with her. So with what would he have recourse upon her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘With half of what he would teach with, similar to that Chapter’.
en.sarwar: 14. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Musa ibn Ja’far from Ahmad ibn Bashir from Ali ibn Asbat from al-Bitkhiy from ibn Bukayr from Zurarah who has said the following: “About the case of a man who marries a woman for teaching her a chapter from the book of Allah, then divorces her before going to bed with her and what she must receive, abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al- Salam, has said, ‘He owes to teach her half as much of that chapter.’”
